story_title: As Technical Support Staff, I want to check whether sufficient suitable equipment is available for an event so that I can determine whether its technical requirements can be supported.

acceptance_criteria.text: The system considers the required equipment type.
The system considers the required quantity.
The system considers the event date and time.
Equipment already reserved for overlapping events is excluded from available quantities.
Equipment is treated as unavailable from its collection day (D-1) through the day after its return (Return Day+1), not only during the event's own date and time.
Required transfer and preparation time between the equipment's current location and the event venue is factored into availability.
Equipment recorded as unavailable is excluded.
The system indicates whether sufficient equipment is available.

open_questions: Test data: every case runs against the seeded database (`npx prisma db seed`, section 'SPM-48 test-case events' in prisma/seed.ts). Event and equipment names, stock and dates are fixed there (Oct 2026 - Jan 2027), so they do not drift with the day the seed is run. Reseeding replaces ALL data in the shared database and logs everyone out. The seed script and this file must be changed together.

The availability screen (S-25) follows design/mockups/EquipmentRequests.dc.html and UI_DESIGN.md section 7.4: availability appears automatically on the request page, with chips 'Available' / 'Partial' / 'Unavailable', the breakdown 'total - in maintenance - reserved elsewhere = N available for these dates', and the banner 'Not everything requested is available.'. There is no separate 'Check availability' button on that page. The transfer note wording ('Leaves ...', 'Already at the venue ...', 'Venue not yet chosen ...') is proposed.

Design decisions assumed by these cases (team proposals; customer Q&A #2, #13, #113 leave them to the team): (a) the fixed 2-hour transfer/prep time applies BEFORE the event only, and only when the equipment is not already at the event venue; nothing is added after the event, so EQUIPMENT_LOAD_WINDOW_MS in equipmentWindowFor() must stop adding 2 hours after the event; (b) Return Day is the event's own end date (automatically populated; Q&A #113 allows this); (c) equipment location is a nullable locationVenueId on Equipment where null means ConnectSphere storage (needs a schema change and migration); (d) an event with no venue yet skips transfer time and shows 'Venue not yet chosen'.

AC5 wording: the Jira text says equipment is unavailable 'through Return Day+1', but the customer (Q&A #5, #2) says it is 'available again from Return Day+1'. These cases follow the customer. The Jira acceptance criterion should be corrected. 'Held by <event> until <date>' is assumed to show the day the equipment is available again (Return Day+1).

Only requests with status 'reserved' or 'partially_fulfilled' count against availability (SCHEMA_REFERENCE.md), using quantityReserved. Requests of cancelled, postponed, rejected and draft events are ignored by a TEMPORARY filter on Event.status (TC08) until SPM-37 (Cancel) and SPM-38 (Postpone) release reservations themselves. Revisit when those stories ship.

Zero total stock (TC01) is shown as 'Unavailable' with 0 available. The team wants different wording from an input error, but the wording is not decided. Requesting zero units (TC04) uses the existing message 'Enter a whole number, at least 1.'.

Retired/inactive equipment (TC20): shown as 'Unavailable' on an existing request and hidden from the Add equipment list, following SPM-39. GET /api/equipment does not filter inactive items today, so the hiding is new behaviour.
Sessions of the same event (TC15): it is not defined whether two sessions of one event, on nearby days, block each other's equipment. No case written.
The 'Reserve what is available' button in the mockup belongs to SPM-49 (Reserve Equipment) and is out of scope for SPM-48. Partial reservation is allowed by the customer (Q&A #90).

AC7: Technical Support can record units as out of service with a reason through PATCH /api/equipment/[id]/out-of-service (the availability check already subtracts them - TC19). There is no screen for it yet: that belongs to SPM-55 (Record Equipment Unavailability), so no manual test case can be written for the recording step. It is covered by unit tests (recordOutOfServiceSchema, checkOutOfService, and the effect on availability). Add cases once SPM-55 provides the screen.
